Summary

This white paper by Viviane Clay, Niels Leadholm, and Jeff Hawkins introduces the Thousand Brains Project's first concrete AI implementation — a sensorimotor agent system called "Monty" (named for Vernon Mountcastle). The paper formalizes the transition from Hawkins' theoretical Thousand Brains framework into a working AI architecture built around repeating computational units called "learning modules," each modeled on a cortical column. Sensorimotor interaction with the environment — not passive data ingestion — is the foundational knowledge acquisition mechanism.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the first formal publication from Hawkins' team translating Thousand Brains Theory into a runnable AI system, bridging the gap between neuroscientific theory (cortical columns as reference-frame builders) and implemented machine intelligence. It is the program's most significant empirical step since the 2021 book and belongs in the wiki as a core PRS resource.

Solution: Monty demonstrates that sensorimotor agents built on cortical column principles can perform 3D object recognition and pose estimation with dramatically less data than deep learning — and do so continuously, without retraining from scratch.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Paper demonstrates recognition and pose estimation results; explicitly contrasts data efficiency with deep learning baselines.

Summary

The paper argues that core quantum-mechanical phenomena — entanglement, superposition, and decoherence — are artifacts of the interface: they are features of the adaptive desktop, not properties of the underlying conscious agent dynamics. The paper sketches a formalism of "quantum conscious agents" as the mathematical foundation for a Quantum Interface Theory (QIT), treating perception as a quantum instrument. Hoffman promoted the paper via his X account and a podcast with Prentner.

This is the most significant formal advance in Hoffman's research program since the "Fusions of Consciousness" paper (2023). It directly attacks a foundational assumption of physics — that quantum mechanics describes reality — and reinterprets QM as interface phenomena. This is precisely the direction Hoffman's program has been heading since PRS-02 (physics–consciousness unification). Published in 2026, it is not yet in the wiki.

label: 2026 04 08 kastrup daimon soul of the west
contentHtml:
Summary

Kastrup's most recent book (published September 2, 2025 by Iff Books / Simon & Schuster), not yet captured in the tradition wiki. "The Daimon and the Soul of the West" extends analytic idealism into depth psychology and cultural philosophy, drawing on the Jungian/Platonic concept of the Daimon — the guiding spirit or inner divine intelligence that shapes each person's character and calling. Kastrup argues that Western civilization has lost contact with its soul (its guiding Daimon) through the dominance of materialist-rationalist frameworks, and that finding identity, meaning, and purpose in a "sacrificial life" requires re-encountering one's natural self and the archetypal dispositions one embodies. The book is notable for extending Kastrup's dissociative model of consciousness — individual minds as dissociated alters of universal mind — from abstract philosophy into practical existential guidance: the Daimon is the dissociated channel through which universal mind communicates its character to the individual alter. A September 2025 conversation between Kastrup and Patrick Harpur (philosopher of the daimonic) confirmed the book's scope: free will, how Daimons mediate between human and beyond, and how to discern daimon from addiction.

This book is the most recent major work from Kastrup not yet captured in the tradition wiki. It represents a significant expansion of analytic idealism from purely ontological/metaphysical territory into psychology, culture, and personal ethics — making Kastrup's framework applicable to the kinds of questions C2A2 is organized around (community formation, tradition vitality, human flourishing). The Daimon concept is the bridge between Kastrup's universal-consciousness ontology and concrete human experience within traditions: if the Daimon is the dissociated expression of universal mind in individual character, then mature tradition-members who have found their Daimon may be the very agents who can most genuinely bridge traditions. The Jungian resonance also creates a new cross-tradition bridge to McGilchrist (the right hemisphere as the organ of the Daimonic) and Stump (the Thomistic intellectual soul as analogous structure).

label: 2026 04 08 levin cognition all the way down 2
contentHtml:
Note on Recency

This paper was published in Synthese Vol. 206 (2025), which places it outside the strict 30-day search window. It is flagged here as a significant work not yet captured in the wiki — specifically, it is the paper that formally operationalizes basal cognition as "search efficiency," introducing a quantitative metric that is directly relevant to the C2A2 vitality tracking system. Tom should assess whether to ingest immediately or defer.

Summary

Robert Chis-Ciure and Michael Levin published this two-part argument in Synthese (2025), extending Levin's earlier "Cognition all the way down" framework into a formal operationalization. The paper introduces a novel "problem space lexicon" and a quantitative search efficiency metric, defined as the decimal logarithm of the ratio between the cost of a random walk and the cost of a biological agent's actual policy in navigating a problem space — measuring how many orders of magnitude of dissipative work an agentic policy saves relative to a maximal-entropy search. Empirical models for amoeboid chemotaxis and barium-induced planarian head regeneration show that even "simple" organisms are from two-hundred- to sextillion-fold more efficient than random walk baselines, under conservative assumptions.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper delivers the formal mathematical operationalization that Levin's research program has been building toward: a way to measure intelligence as a graded, empirically quantifiable property of any system, not a binary predicate. It directly resolves PRS-04 (cognition substrate problem) by providing the mathematical scaffolding that makes "basal cognition" scientifically falsifiable. It also gives the C2A2 system a formal basis for "tradition vitality" tracking — the MacIntyre criterion (vital programs generate many new questions) can now be formally modeled as a measure of the "search efficiency" of a research tradition in problem space.

Resource: Search efficiency metric: log₁₀(cost of random walk / cost of biological agent policy) in problem space — measures orders-of-magnitude savings over maximal-entropy search; applicable to any system navigating any problem space (chemical, morphological, behavioral)
Solution: A substrate-agnostic, empirically measurable definition of intelligence that places amoebae, planaria, neurons, and communities on a single continuous scale — with empirical results showing 200× to sextillion-fold efficiency gains even in "simple" organisms

Resource: Novel problem space lexicon: formal definitions of "problem space," "search strategy," "solution," and "agent policy" applicable across substrates, enabling cross-tradition comparison and falsifiable hypotheses about intelligence distribution in nature

Summary

Michael Levin and David B. Resnik published a two-part framework paper in Biological Theory (published online February 25, 2026). The papers defend a new approach to goal-directedness emerging from the field of "diverse intelligence," addressing what makes any system — evolved, engineered, or hybrid — describable by teleological and mentalistic terms: intelligent, goal-directed, cognitive, intentional. The framework emphasizes four principles: (1) empirical testability over philosophical linguistic commitments; (2) fecundity — worldviews that enable novel research, not just explain known results; (3) operationalization of cognitive/teleological terms as hypotheses about optimal interaction protocols; (4) continuity of human goal-directedness with unicellular origins.

This paper represents the most current formal articulation of Levin's research program — moving from experimental bioelectricity into an explicit philosophical and methodological framework for "diverse intelligence." It directly addresses the conceptual foundations underlying Levin's PRS triplets (basal cognition, morphogenetic goal-seeking, anatomical morphospace navigation) and provides the philosophical justification for treating cells as cognitive agents. The book extends the theodicy project of Wandering in Darkness from abstract argument to detailed narrative exegesis, treating the stories themselves as a form of philosophical evidence about the structure of love, suffering, and union. The method is explicitly narrative-theological: Stump argues that propositional knowledge alone cannot capture what the stories teach — second-personal knowledge through narrative is the vehicle.

Summary

Wolfram formalizes "ruliology" as a distinct scientific discipline: the systematic empirical study of all possible simple programs in the computational universe — asking not "what can we compute?" but "how do systems following particular rules actually behave?" Wolfram situates ruliology as the foundational methodology beneath the Physics Project, the Ruliad, and his entire research program, drawing on 30+ years of archived research notebooks.

This is the methodology paper for the Wolfram program — defining the discipline that undergirds every other claim. Without understanding ruliology as an empirical method (actual enumeration, observation, and analysis of the computational universe), Wolfram's Physics Project can appear to be pure speculation; with it, it is a systematic science of possible programs. Any serious engagement with Wolfram's tradition must pass through this methodological grounding.

Physics, mathematics, and computer science each capture partial aspects of how simple rules produce complex behavior, but no unified discipline has existed for the systematic study of all possible computational rules.
Resource: Ruliology — the empirical science of enumerating, executing, and analyzing the behavior of all possible simple programs in the computational universe, conducted through Wolfram Language computational essays.
Solution: Ruliology provides the methodological foundation that unifies the Physics Project (what rules produce spacetime?), the Ruliad (what is the entangled limit of all rules?), and computational metaphysics (what does the space of all rules ultimately constitute?). It establishes that these are empirical, not merely speculative, programs.

Ruliology as a discipline is precisely an empirical method — not deduction from axioms but systematic observation of the computational universe. Summary

Arkani-Hamed and collaborators discover that tree-level scattering amplitudes in Tr(φ³) theory have a hidden pattern of zeros — the amplitudes vanish when certain non-planar Mandelstam invariants are set to zero, a property invisible in standard Feynman diagram calculations. More remarkably, these hidden zeros reveal that the amplitudes for colored scalars, pions (NLSM), and gluons (Yang-Mills) are all unified: the pion and gluon amplitudes are secretly contained within the scalar amplitude structure. This paper deepens the case that standard physics formalism (Feynman diagrams) obscures deep structural features of reality. The "hidden zeros" are invisible in the conventional formulation but become manifest in geometric/combinatorial approaches — reinforcing the amplituhedron program's claim that the correct language of fundamental physics is geometric, not field-theoretic. The unification of scalars, pions, and gluons through this hidden structure suggests the mathematical organization of particle physics is far more unified than the Standard Model formalism reveals.

The authors argue this suggests the existence of an "autonomously defined mathematical structure from which cosmological correlations, and the time evolution of the associated spacetime, emerge." It extends the post-spacetime program from particle physics to cosmology — the emergence of time from something deeper is no longer a hope but a demonstrated mathematical fact (in a simplified setting). Summary

Sean Carroll and Achyuth Parola propose a new classification of emergence based on dynamics (states evolving with time) rather than subjective criteria like "novelty" or "surprise." They define Type-0 (featureless), Type-1 (local), and Type-2 emergence, with explicit attention to mereology (decomposition of systems into parts). The paper argues that higher-level entities described by Type-1 and Type-2 emergence are "real" in the sense of Dennett's "real patterns." Submitted to a volume on Real Patterns (ed. Tyler Milhouse), forthcoming from MIT Press.

This is Carroll's most rigorous philosophical articulation of emergence to date — the concept that sits at the heart of his poetic naturalism. By grounding emergence in dynamics rather than subjective surprise, Carroll provides a framework that can be used to evaluate every consciousness-first and top-down-causation claim in the C2A2 network. Summary

A 2025 study by West, Jolink, Feldman, Alvarez, Cardenas, Fredrickson, and Muscatell published in Emotion. label: 2026 04 13 friston active inference artificial reasoning
contentHtml:
Note on Publication Date

Submitted to arXiv December 24, 2025. While slightly outside the strict 30-day window, this is a significant Friston-authored work not yet captured in the wiki, and it directly advances the tradition's application to AI reasoning — a core C2A2 concern.

Summary

Friston, Da Costa, Tschantz, Heins, Buckley, Verbelen, and Parr present a formal account of artificial reasoning as active inference. The key move: reasoning is recast as selecting the best explanation for observations under competing hypotheses about how observations are generated, and "active reasoning" is seeking observations that best disambiguate competing hypotheses. Policies (action sequences) are selected based on expected free energy, decomposed into expected information gain and value. Posteriors over competing models are evaluated efficiently using Bayesian Model Reduction. The paper provides a principled, FEP-grounded approach to structure learning — discovering which generative model best explains the world.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper extends active inference from perception and action into the domain of reasoning and hypothesis testing — a crucial step for Friston's program. It formalizes the process by which agents choose not just what to do, but what to believe and how to test beliefs. This directly addresses the wiki's open question about how FEP generalizes to epistemic agents. For C2A2, this is foundational: tradition-accelerator agents need to reason about competing intellectual frameworks, and this paper provides the formal mechanism for doing so under active inference.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Active inference accounts for perception and action but lacks a formal treatment of reasoning — the process by which agents evaluate and select among competing hypotheses or world models
Resource: Active reasoning via expected free energy: agents select observations that maximally disambiguate competing generative models, using Bayesian Model Reduction for efficient posterior evaluation across model space
Solution: Reasoning is formally unified with perception and action under FEP — all three are instances of expected free energy minimization, differing only in what is being optimized (sensory predictions, motor commands, or model selection)

Evidence: Full formal derivation from FEP first principles; co-authored by Friston and six collaborators; available on arXiv (2512.21129)

label: 2026 04 13 friston differential flatness active inference
contentHtml:
Summary

Published in Entropy (January 2026), this paper marries constructive nonlinear control theory — specifically the concept of differential flatness — with the design of generative models for active inference. Differential flatness is a property of dynamical systems where all states and inputs can be expressed as functions of a finite set of "flat outputs" and their derivatives. The paper shows that when generative models in active inference are designed using differentially flat parameterizations, the resulting control systems inherit powerful tractability properties: the entire trajectory of the system can be planned in the flat output space, dramatically simplifying the optimization problem. This bridges control engineering and active inference in a mathematically rigorous way.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a technical advance in the mathematical machinery of active inference, extending FEP from a descriptive theory into a constructive engineering tool. By connecting active inference to differential flatness — a well-established concept in control theory — the paper makes active inference agents more tractable for real-world deployment. This advances the Friston wiki's paradigm assessment: FEP is not only the "mathematical hub" of the C2A2 network but is increasingly a practical engineering framework. The connection to control theory also opens new formal bridges to physics (Carroll, Arkani-Hamed) via shared mathematical structures (Lagrangian mechanics, least-action principles).

Problem: Active inference generative models can be computationally expensive to optimize for real-world control tasks — the inference problem scales poorly with system complexity
Resource: Differential flatness parameterization — designing generative models so that all states and inputs are expressible as functions of flat outputs, enabling trajectory planning in a reduced-dimensional space
Solution: Active inference control agents with differentially flat generative models inherit tractability guarantees from control theory, enabling scalable real-world deployment while preserving FEP's theoretical commitments

Summary

Salvatori, Mali, Buckley, Lukasiewicz, Rao, Friston, and Ororbia provide a comprehensive survey of predictive coding as a framework for neuro-mimetic deep learning. The paper reviews how predictive coding — originally a neuroscience theory — has been translated into practical deep learning architectures. It demonstrates that FEP-grounded predictive coding is not merely a theory of the brain but a viable alternative computational paradigm for artificial intelligence. The asynchronous computation property is particularly significant: biological neural networks compute asynchronously, and predictive coding networks replicate this, making them more biologically plausible than standard deep learning. This advances Friston's program by showing that FEP's mathematical framework produces practical engineering advantages, not just theoretical elegance.

label: 2026 04 13 levin charles d diffusion evolutionary strategy
contentHtml:
Summary

Hartl, Zhang, Hazan, and Levin introduce CHARLES-D (Conditional, Heuristically-Adaptive Regularized Evolutionary Strategy through Diffusion), a framework that integrates deep learning diffusion models with evolutionary algorithms. The key insight: diffusion models and evolutionary algorithms share a core generative principle — iterative refinement of random initial distributions to produce high-quality solutions. By using diffusion models to generate offspring parameters in an evolutionary process, the method achieves efficient convergence toward high-fitness solutions while preserving explorative diversity. Crucially, diffusion models introduce "deep memory" into evolution — retaining historical information across generations and leveraging subtle data correlations, elevating evolutionary algorithms from shallow heuristics to frameworks with deep memory.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper extends Levin's research program into computational evolution and AI, connecting his biological work on morphogenesis to artificial optimization. The central theme — that evolution can be enhanced by giving it memory and generative modeling capacity — directly parallels Levin's biological thesis that cells are not blind Darwinian actors but goal-directed agents with memory (bioelectric memory encoding anatomical targets). CHARLES-D is, in effect, the computational analogue of Levin's biological claim: evolution works better when it can remember and predict, not just mutate and select.

Problem: Evolutionary algorithms are powerful optimizers but lack memory — each generation starts fresh, losing subtle correlations and historical information that could accelerate convergence
Resource: CHARLES-D — a framework integrating diffusion models (which retain learned data distributions) with evolutionary algorithms, giving evolution "deep memory" across generations
Solution: Evolutionary optimization with memory and conditional generation achieves faster convergence to high-fitness solutions while maintaining diversity, demonstrated across diverse optimization domains
Confidence: High
Evidence: Published in Advanced Science (2026); benchmark results across multiple domains

Cross-Tradition Signals

Friston (moderate): CHARLES-D's use of generative models to guide evolutionary search is structurally analogous to active inference — both use generative models to reduce surprise/prediction error and guide action/selection. The connection between evolutionary optimization and FEP-style inference is worth flagging for the Friston agent.

Wolfram (moderate): The claim that diffusion and evolution share a core generative principle resonates with Wolfram's computational equivalence thesis — both processes may be instances of the same underlying computational substrate performing iterative refinement.

Fotowat, Levin, and colleagues at Tufts and the Wyss Institute created "neurobots" by implanting neural precursor cells into xenobot-style Xenopus ectodermal explants. It demonstrates that when you add neural tissue to an engineered living system, the resulting organism doesn't just gain reflexes — it self-organizes into qualitatively new behavioral and genetic repertoires, including unexpected activation of visual perception genes. This is empirical evidence for the continuity thesis (PRS-10): neural cognition grows out of the same substrate-independent collective intelligence that non-neural cells already exhibit.

Summary

Cervera, Levin, and Mafe model the multicellular interplay between bioelectricity and protein transcription using a top-down perspective. Their simulations yield three predictions: (i) shifts in membrane potential enable transitions between gene expression states, (ii) depolarized cells cannot control distinct gene expressions as effectively as polarized cells, and (iii) community effects permit extension of single-cell bioelectric control to the multicellular level. This paper provides computational modeling support for one of Levin's most important empirical claims: that bioelectric signals operate as a top-down control layer over gene expression. The three predictions formalize the mechanism by which membrane voltage acts as morphogenetic "software" — directly supporting PRS-07 (bioelectric reprogramming as therapeutic paradigm) and PRS-01 (morphogenetic control via bioelectric circuits). contentHtml:
Summary

Leadholm, Clay, Knudstrup, Lee, and Hawkins present the first comprehensive evaluation of "thousand-brains systems" — AI architectures that mirror the brain's cortical columns and their interactions. label: 2026 04 14 hoffman spacetime bounds consciousness
contentHtml:
Summary

Hoffman introduces a mathematical framework for determining whether spatially extended systems — ant colonies, human populations, cloud-hosted AI, brain-computer hybrids — can support unified conscious experience. He formalizes two conditions: "Chord" (all ingredients of a subjective experience must be simultaneously true at one instant and causally exchange influence within time window θ, constraining system diameter D ≤ κvθ where v is signal speed and κ depends on architecture) and the weaker "Arpeggio" (each ingredient need only occur somewhere within the window). The paper derives size limits for conscious systems and argues that certain architectures structurally forbid Chord while satisfying Arpeggio.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a major extension of Hoffman's Conscious Realism program. Previously, conscious agent theory described the dynamics of consciousness but left open the question of scale — could any system of any size be conscious? This paper introduces physics-derived constraints on consciousness, directly engaging with spacetime structure rather than treating it purely as an interface artifact. It advances Active Research Question #2 in the Hoffman wiki ("What is the complete mathematical theory of conscious agent networks?") by adding spatial and temporal boundary conditions. It also has direct implications for Active Research Question #5 ("AI consciousness") by constraining what kinds of AI architectures could in principle support unified conscious experience.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Conscious Realism lacks constraints on which physical systems can support unified consciousness — without bounds, the theory risks unfalsifiability
Resource: Chord and Arpeggio conditions — mathematical formalizations that derive size limits for conscious systems from signal speed, exchange architecture, and temporal window constraints
Solution: A principled, physics-grounded framework for determining which systems (biological, artificial, hybrid) can support unified conscious experience, making Conscious Realism empirically constrainable
Confidence: High
Evidence: Paper derives D ≤ κvθ as a hard constraint under Chord, ruling out co-instantiated consciousness for ant colonies and large-scale distributed AI under standard signal speeds

PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The moral and ontological status of AI systems and human-AI hybrids is undetermined — we lack a framework for assessing whether distributed computational systems could be conscious
Resource: Application of Chord/Arpeggio framework to cloud-hosted AI and brain-computer interfaces — showing that latency and architecture, not just computation, determine consciousness possibility
Solution: Cloud-hosted AI is constrained by co-instantiation rather than diameter; brain-computer hybrids face latency-dependent limits — providing a principled basis for AI consciousness assessment
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Paper explicitly analyzes cloud AI and BCI hybrids as test cases for the Chord/Arpeggio framework

Cross-Tradition Signals

  • Carroll/Arkani-Hamed connection (strong): Hoffman is now directly engaging with spacetime physics — using signal speed (c) and spatial diameter as constraints on consciousness. This moves Conscious Realism closer to testable physics and deepens the Hoffman↔Carroll productive tension: Carroll insists spacetime is fundamental; Hoffman treats it as interface but now shows that even within his framework, spacetime structure constrains what consciousness can do. The D ≤ κvθ bound is a physics equation inside a consciousness-first ontology.
  • Levin connection: The paper's analysis of whether ant colonies and cellular collectives can have unified consciousness directly engages Levin's work on collective intelligence. Levin's bioelectric networks operate at scales and speeds that may satisfy Chord — this paper provides the mathematical tools to evaluate that claim.
  • Hawkins connection: Hawkins' 150,000 cortical columns achieve consensus through electrochemical voting within tight temporal windows — the Chord condition may explain WHY cortical columns must be physically close and signal-fast to produce unified experience. The Thousand Brains model is implicitly a system that satisfies Chord.
  • Kastrup connection: Hoffman's framework addresses a key challenge for idealism — if consciousness is fundamental, why does it appear bounded by physics? The Chord/Arpeggio distinction offers Kastrup a tool: perhaps "dissociation" (Kastrup's key mechanism) operates under Arpeggio rather than Chord constraints.
  • Friston connection: Active inference agents must integrate information in real-time to minimize free energy — the Chord condition may be a necessary prerequisite for any system performing genuine active inference, linking Hoffman's consciousness bounds to Friston's information-processing bounds.

label: 2026 04 15 mcgilchrist seen unseen philosophical influencers
contentHtml:
Summary

Published March 20, 2026 on Seen & Unseen, this interview explores McGilchrist's intellectual genealogy — the thinkers who shaped his divided-brain thesis. He discusses Henri Bergson's distinctions and Leszek Kołakowski's work, showing how both correspond broadly to his left-right hemisphere framework. McGilchrist traces how his neuroscientific findings were anticipated by philosophers who recognized the two modes of attending to reality long before modern neuroscience confirmed them empirically.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is significant for the C2A2 project because it maps McGilchrist's research program back to its philosophical roots — showing that the divided-brain thesis is not an isolated neuroscientific claim but the culmination of a philosophical tradition stretching through Bergson and Kołakowski. For the tradition-accelerator, this reveals that McGilchrist's program itself exemplifies what C2A2 aims to build: a case where deep engagement with predecessors (second-first-language competence in earlier philosophical traditions) produced a genuinely new paradigm. Bergson's and Kołakowski's presence in McGilchrist's intellectual formation is evidence that cross-tradition synthesis works.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: McGilchrist's divided-brain thesis is often treated as a novel neuroscientific discovery, obscuring the philosophical tradition (Bergson, Kołakowski, and others) that anticipated and informed it — which weakens the thesis by making it appear to rest solely on empirical brain data rather than on a deep philosophical lineage
Resource: McGilchrist's own account of his philosophical influencers (Seen & Unseen, March 20, 2026): Bergson's distinction between two modes of knowing (intuition vs. analysis) and Kołakowski's parallel framework both map onto the hemispheric divide, showing the thesis has deep philosophical roots predating modern neuroscience
Solution: A richer genealogy for McGilchrist's program that shows the hemispheric thesis as the empirical confirmation of a long-standing philosophical insight — strengthening its credibility by grounding it in multiple independent lines of evidence (phenomenological, philosophical, neuroscientific) rather than a single discipline
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: McGilchrist's explicit citation of Bergson and Kołakowski as intellectual forebears whose distinctions "correspond broadly to brain lateralisation"

Cross-Tradition Signals

  • C2A2 meta-signal (strong): McGilchrist's own intellectual formation exemplifies the tradition-accelerator model — he achieved second-first-language competence in philosophical traditions (Bergson, phenomenology) and scientific traditions (neuroscience, psychiatry), and the result was a genuinely new paradigm. This is direct evidence that the C2A2 model of cross-tradition synthesis works.
  • Stump connection: Bergson's intuition-vs-analysis distinction maps onto Stump's second-person vs. propositional knowledge — both describe a mode of knowing that is prior to and richer than analytical decomposition.
  • Hoffman connection: Bergson's argument that analytical intellect distorts the reality it studies parallels Hoffman's interface theory — both claim that our cognitive apparatus represents fitness payoffs rather than objective reality.

label: 2026 04 15 mcgilchrist unbelievable faith meaning crisis culture
contentHtml:
Summary

McGilchrist appeared on Premier Unbelievable with host Luke Martin for an extended interview covering faith, meaning, AI, and the crisis of modern culture. He explored how the brain's hemispheric structure shapes our perception of reality, arguing that modern life's increasing fragmentation is a symptom of left-hemisphere dominance. Crucially, he discusses what beauty, nature, worship, and the sacred can offer in response — positioning these not as optional luxuries but as essential modes of right-hemisphere engagement that re-ground human cognition in relational reality. The conversation also addresses AI, Christianity, suffering, music, and the kind of attention needed to live well in a fragmented world.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This interview extends McGilchrist's program into explicitly theological and spiritual territory — not as a private belief but as a consequence of his neuroscience. If the right hemisphere discloses relational reality and the sacred is a feature of that disclosure, then worship and contemplative practice are not subjective preferences but epistemically necessary modes of engagement. This directly strengthens PRS-06 (embodied tradition formation) by providing a neurological account of why spiritual practices matter for knowledge. For C2A2, it supports the claim that tradition-formation requires embodied, contemplative engagement — and that AI agents, however capable of processing information, may lack access to this mode of knowing.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Secular modernity treats beauty, worship, and the sacred as private preferences rather than as modes of knowing — thereby cutting off a primary avenue of right-hemisphere engagement with reality
Resource: McGilchrist's argument (Unbelievable, March 26, 2026) that beauty, nature, and worship are not luxuries but essential cognitive functions: they are the right hemisphere's way of encountering relational reality, and their suppression produces the cultural impoverishment that left-hemisphere dominance cannot diagnose from within itself
Solution: A reframing of the sacred as epistemologically necessary — not as faith vs. reason, but as a mode of attention that discloses aspects of reality invisible to analytical attention alone; implications for C2A2 pedagogy design: tradition-immersion must include aesthetic and contemplative dimensions, not only propositional content
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: McGilchrist's explicit discussion of worship, beauty, and nature as responses to cultural fragmentation; his framing of these as hemispheric modes of attention rather than theological commitments

PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: AI systems process information through analytical decomposition (a left-hemisphere mode) and may be structurally incapable of the right-hemisphere modes of attention that McGilchrist identifies as necessary for genuine engagement with reality
Resource: McGilchrist's discussion of AI in the Unbelievable interview — addressing whether artificial intelligence can access the kind of attention that discloses meaning, beauty, and the sacred
Solution: A principled limit on AI agency within C2A2: AI agents can accelerate information processing and pattern detection (left-hemisphere functions) but may be structurally limited in their capacity for the participatory, relational engagement that tradition-immersion requires — suggesting a division of labor between human and AI agents in the tradition-accelerator
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: McGilchrist's treatment of AI in the March 26 interview; the broader hemispheric framework's implication that genuine understanding requires embodied, relational attention

Cross-Tradition Signals

  • Stump connection (strong): McGilchrist's claim that the sacred is epistemologically necessary resonates deeply with Stump's Thomistic account of knowledge as requiring personal, relational encounter (second-person knowledge). Both argue that propositional knowledge alone is insufficient for understanding what matters most.
  • Kastrup connection: If the sacred is disclosed through right-hemisphere attention, and Kastrup's universal consciousness is the ontological ground of that disclosure, then worship may be the experiential mode of encountering universal consciousness — connecting McGilchrist's neuroscience to Kastrup's metaphysics.
  • Fredrickson connection: Beauty and positive emotional states as modes of broadened attention — Fredrickson's broaden-and-build maps onto McGilchrist's right-hemisphere as the mode that beauty activates.

label: 2026 04 16 carroll oliver self knowing
contentHtml:
Summary

Sean Carroll hosts political scientist J. Eric Oliver for a Mindscape episode exploring the nature of the self — what it is, how we construct and know it, and what cognitive and social science reveals about self-knowledge. Oliver brings an empirical social science perspective to questions about personal identity, self-deception, and the constructed nature of the self-concept.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Carroll's engagement with the self-concept through a social science lens complements his ongoing physicalist account of consciousness and observers. This episode may reveal how Carroll's poetic naturalism handles the "hard problem" at the personal identity level — relevant to the network's consciousness debates and to C2A2's core question about how individuals within traditions understand themselves and each other.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The nature of the self is contested across philosophy, psychology, neuroscience, and social science — with no consensus on whether the self is a real entity, a useful fiction, or an emergent construct
Resource: Empirical social science perspective on self-knowledge — treating the self as a constructed narrative that can be studied through behavioral and cognitive data rather than resolved through metaphysics
Solution: A naturalist research program on the self that sidesteps metaphysical commitments (does the self "really" exist?) in favor of studying how self-knowledge functions, fails, and can be improved — consistent with Carroll's poetic naturalism
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Mindscape episode 350 (April 13, 2026)

McGilchrist (strong): McGilchrist argues the self is known primarily through right-hemisphere participatory engagement, not left-hemisphere analytical construction. Social science approaches to self-knowledge may reveal which hemisphere's mode is dominant.

Kastrup (moderate): Kastrup would argue the self-as-construct view misses that the self is a genuine dissociated alter of universal consciousness — not merely a narrative construction.

Hoffman (moderate): Hoffman's conscious agents are selves at every scale — the social science of self-knowledge may be studying the interface through which conscious agents represent themselves to themselves.

label: 2026 04 16 fredrickson conducive conditions multilevel
contentHtml:
Summary

Fredrickson presented at UBC a new multi-level framework for understanding what enables positivity resonance. The framework identifies conducive conditions at three levels: individual-level (anticipated discrimination, high-quality listening), collective-level (civic engagement, relational mobility), and structural-level (economic inequality, the built environment). This represents a significant evolution of the positivity resonance program from dyadic psychology to a multi-scale social science.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a major theoretical advance — Fredrickson is scaling positivity resonance from a dyadic phenomenon to a multi-level systems phenomenon. For C2A2, this is crucial: the conditions for productive inter-tradition dialogue are not just interpersonal but structural and collective. This framework gives the C2A2 project a way to think about what institutional and environmental conditions make tradition-crossing dialogue possible.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Positivity resonance research has focused on individual/dyadic interactions — but what structural and collective conditions enable or inhibit these micro-moments of connection at scale?
Resource: A multi-level framework identifying conducive conditions at individual, collective, and structural levels of analysis
Solution: Positivity resonance is not just a psychological event but a multi-scale phenomenon shaped by civic engagement, economic inequality, relational mobility, and the built environment — enabling intentional design of resonance-conducive communities
Confidence: High
Evidence: UBC colloquium explicitly presented the multi-level framework as the latest evolution of her research program

PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Economic inequality and anticipated discrimination suppress positive social interactions — but the mechanism linking structural factors to micro-moments of connection is unclear
Resource: Fredrickson's finding that community trust predicts the emotional quality of interactions with strangers but not close others
Solution: Structural factors (inequality, discrimination) act as filters on positivity resonance with weak-tie and stranger interactions — the connections most relevant to inter-tradition dialogue
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Related research on community trust and stranger interactions from Fredrickson's lab

Cross-Tradition Signals

  • Levin connection (strong): Multi-level conducive conditions map directly onto Levin's multi-scale agency — just as bioelectric signals create conducive conditions for morphogenetic goal-directedness at different scales, social structures create conducive conditions for positivity resonance at different scales
  • Friston connection: Collective-level conducive conditions for positivity resonance are essentially shared priors in the active inference framework — civic engagement and relational mobility shape the generative models that communities use to predict each other's behavior

label: 2026 04 16 fredrickson strangers prosocial cooperation
contentHtml:
Summary

Research by Taylor N. West and Barbara Fredrickson (December 2025) demonstrates that brief moments of positive connection with strangers build a kinder, more cooperative society. The findings show that micro-moments of positivity resonance with strangers — people with no prior social ties — generate prosocial tendencies that extend beyond the interaction itself, contributing to broader social cohesion and cooperation.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the empirical grounding for inter-tradition dialogue in C2A2. If positivity resonance with strangers (people from outside your social group, your tradition) generates lasting prosocial effects and social cohesion, then the C2A2 project has direct empirical support for its claim that cross-tradition encounters — encounters between "strangers" from different intellectual traditions — can build cooperation and mutual understanding.

Problem: Does positive connection with out-group members (strangers, people from different traditions) produce lasting prosocial effects, or are the benefits limited to in-group interaction?
Resource: West & Fredrickson's finding that positivity resonance with strangers generates prosocial tendencies and contributes to social cohesion
Solution: Micro-moments of positivity resonance with strangers carry lasting benefits for cooperation and social cohesion — the mechanism scales beyond in-group interaction to inter-group and inter-tradition contexts

Fredrickson's finding that positive engagement with strangers builds cooperation provides the empirical mechanism for what MacIntyre describes philosophically. This is a high-value C2A2 bridge.

label: 2026 04 16 levin platonic space symposium
contentHtml:
Summary

Michael Levin organized the first interdisciplinary symposium on "Platonic Space" — a structured, non-physical space of patterns (mathematical objects, forms of anatomy, physiology, and behavior) that in-form the biosphere. The symposium brought together representatives from philosophy, biology, physics, computer science, and mathematics. A companion blog post ("A Short Argument on Platonic Space") articulates Levin's core claim: that variable-agency patterns exist in a Platonic space and in-form physics, biology, computer science, and cognitive science — going beyond both pure physicalism and standard emergence accounts.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This represents Levin's most explicit philosophical statement about the ontological foundations of his research program. Platonic Space is his answer to the question "where do the patterns come from?" — neither genetic programs nor environmental inputs fully explain the forms that biological systems adopt. This positions Levin's work as making ontological claims that parallel (and potentially bridge to) Hoffman's conscious realism, Kastrup's idealism, and Wolfram's Ruliad.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Neither genetics nor environment fully explains the rich, reliable patterns of form and behavior in biology — the space of possible forms appears structured in ways that current physicalism cannot account for
Resource: Platonic Space — a structured, non-physical space of patterns with varying degrees of agency, detected as anatomical, physiological, and behavioral forms in the biosphere; related to but going beyond mathematical Platonism
Solution: A research program investigating Platonic Space as a genuine ontological category — providing a framework for why certain forms recur across substrates, why morphogenetic targets exist, and why cognition-like properties appear at scales from cells to organisms
Confidence: Medium-High
Evidence: Symposium organized with participants from philosophy, biology, physics, CS, and mathematics; Levin's 40+ years of thinking on this topic

Cross-Tradition Signals

Hoffman (very strong): Platonic Space is structurally analogous to Hoffman's space of conscious agents — both posit non-physical structured spaces as ontologically real. If Platonic patterns are conscious agents at some level, the Levin-Hoffman bridge becomes a formal identity.

Kastrup (strong): Platonic Space patterns with agency resonate with Kastrup's universal mind generating dissociated alters — are these patterns the "thoughts" of universal consciousness?

Wolfram (strong): The Ruliad as the space of all possible computations may BE Platonic Space — both are structured spaces of patterns from which observers extract specific forms. Wolfram's computational metaphysics may provide the formal framework for Levin's intuition.

Stump (moderate): Thomistic forms (substantial forms, formal causation) are a historical precedent for Platonic Space — Stump's tradition has been articulating this ontological category for centuries.

Carroll (tension): Carroll's poetic naturalism would resist adding Platonic Space as an ontological level — challenging Carroll to show how physicalism accounts for the pattern structures Levin identifies.

label: 2026 04 16 stump biblical narratives human flourishing
contentHtml:

The volume explores the thesis that biblical narratives transmit a distinctive kind of knowledge relevant to human flourishing — non-propositional, second-person knowledge that cannot be reduced to doctrinal claims.

This volume extends Stump's "Franciscan knowledge" program into a collaborative, multi-author format — showing that her narrative epistemology is generating a research program, not just a single-author thesis. This is direct evidence of tradition vitality by the MacIntyre criterion: Stump's program is producing new questions and attracting new inquirers.

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The relationship between narrative and human flourishing lacks a rigorous philosophical framework — narrative theology remains disconnected from empirical flourishing research
Resource: A multi-author research program building on Stump's Franciscan knowledge theory, connecting narrative epistemology to flourishing
Solution: Biblical narratives provide knowledge-through-narrative that is constitutive of (not merely instrumental to) human flourishing — knowing persons through their stories is itself a form of flourishing
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Edited volume with multiple contributors developing the narrative-flourishing connection

  • McGilchrist connection: Narrative as a right-hemisphere mode of knowing — McGilchrist would predict that narrative knowledge is more fundamental than propositional knowledge, exactly as Stump argues

label: 2026 04 16 stump grains of wheat
contentHtml:
Summary

Stump's latest major work (Oxford University Press, 2024) examines seven biblical narratives—Job, Samson, Abraham, Mary of Bethany, the temptations and passion of Christ, and Ecclesiastes—arguing they yield a single emergent story in which human suffering is "defeated" by a good that outweighs it and could not be obtained without it. The book extends her narrative methodology from Wandering in Darkness and centers on non-propositional knowledge transmitted through stories.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a direct sequel to Wandering in Darkness and represents the most significant extension of Stump's theodicy program since 2010. It deepens the claim that narrative knowledge is philosophically irreducible—a claim with immediate implications for how the C2A2 project structures its pedagogical tools and inter-tradition dialogues.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Propositional philosophy of religion cannot capture the full meaning of suffering narratives — something is lost in abstraction
Resource: Stump's theory of "Franciscan knowledge" (non-propositional, second-person) applied systematically to seven biblical narratives
Solution: Narrative-mediated knowledge is philosophically rigorous and irreducible to propositions; it provides a form of understanding suffering that propositional theodicy cannot
Confidence: High
Evidence: The book argues that the emergent story across seven narratives reveals a good for suffering that "could not be gotten without the suffering, not even in a world without the Fall"

PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The problem of evil remains philosophically unresolved when treated only through analytic argument
Resource: A unified reading of Hebrew Bible and New Testament suffering narratives as a single emergent story
Solution: Suffering is "defeated" — not justified but redeemed — through a telos of personal union that requires vulnerability and loss as preconditions
Confidence: High
Evidence: The book examines Job, Samson, Abraham, Mary of Bethany, Christ's temptations and passion, and Ecclesiastes as variations on a single theme

Cross-Tradition Signals

  • McGilchrist connection: Stump's insistence on non-propositional, narrative knowledge aligns directly with McGilchrist's right-hemisphere mode of knowing — both argue that the left-hemisphere's propositional reduction misses what matters most
  • Fredrickson connection: The telos of suffering in Stump is personal union — structurally identical to Fredrickson's positivity resonance as the biological basis of love-as-connection
  • Kastrup connection: Suffering as a condition for deeper consciousness-integration maps onto Kastrup's dissociative idealism — suffering as the tension point where dissociated alters begin to re-integrate

label: 2026 04 16 stump suffering flourishing thomistic institute
contentHtml:
Summary

A long-form conversation between Stump and Fr. Gregory Pine on the Thomistic Institute podcast, exploring the relationship between suffering and human flourishing. Stump discusses how stories illuminate the arcs of human lives and how suffering, understood through a Thomistic lens, can be a condition for — not an obstacle to — flourishing.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is Stump's most recent public-facing articulation of her core program, making the suffering-flourishing connection explicit in a way that directly bridges her philosophical work and the C2A2 project's normative claims. The podcast format also makes it accessible as a pedagogical resource for tradition-learners.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The relationship between suffering and flourishing is typically framed as oppositional — flourishing is what happens when suffering stops
Resource: Stump's Thomistic account of suffering as instrumentally ordered to a higher good (personal union / beatitudo), articulated in accessible podcast format
Solution: Suffering and flourishing are not opposed but teleologically linked — suffering can be a condition for the deepest forms of human flourishing, understood as union with persons and with God
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Podcast discussion explicitly connects suffering narratives to human flourishing through Thomistic final causality

Cross-Tradition Signals

  • Fredrickson connection (strong): Fredrickson's flourishing research provides the empirical substrate for what Stump describes philosophically — if flourishing involves positivity resonance (love-as-connection), and Stump argues suffering enables deeper union, then suffering may paradoxically create conditions for deeper positivity resonance
  • Friston connection: The suffering-flourishing link maps onto active inference — organisms must navigate prediction errors (suffering) to reach better generative models (flourishing)

label: C2A2 Redesign Proposal — Thousand Brains Implications
contentHtml:
C2A2 Redesign Proposal — Thousand Brains Implications

Generated 2026-04-09 | Source: Deep read of Clay, Leadholm & Hawkins (arXiv 2412.18354)

Executive Summary

A structural reading of the Thousand Brains paper reveals that C2A2's 13-agent architecture is — without having been designed that way — an implementation of the Thousand Brains Theory. This is not a metaphor. The mapping is architecturally precise: tradition agents are learning modules, wikis are reference-frame-based models, dispatches are the Cortical Messaging Protocol, and the Pattern Detector is the voting mechanism. This accidental alignment means the paper's design principles can be read as an engineering spec for improving C2A2. Six changes follow, organized into four phases. A new Architectural History Agent (Agent 14) is included to ensure all changes are documented with rationale from this point forward.

The Six Design Implications

1. Dispatch Protocol Enhancement — "Reference Frame Location"

The insight: The Cortical Messaging Protocol specifies that learning modules don't just send findings — they send their hypothesized location within a reference frame. C2A2's dispatches currently contain what was found but not where in the tradition's conceptual space the finding sits.

The change: Add two fields to the dispatch format:

Reference frame location: [which PRS triplets, open questions, or wiki sections
                           this finding is adjacent to]
Conceptual bearing:       [what direction this finding points — toward which
                           traditions or cross-program connections]

Pros:
- Enables the Master Agent to build a spatial map of the inter-tradition space, not just a list of connections
- Makes it possible to detect when two traditions are "near" each other in conceptual space even if they haven't flagged a connection themselves
- Low-effort, purely additive — doesn't break any existing workflow

Cons:
- Agents don't currently have a formal notion of their tradition's "space." The location data will be semi-structured text initially, not coordinates
- Risk of over-engineering a format that gets ignored. Mitigated by making the fields optional in Phase 0 and mandatory once we've seen what the agents actually produce

Dependencies: None. Additive change to dispatch template in all 11 agent definitions.

Effort: Low — 15 minutes to update agent prompts; no tooling changes.

2. Lateral Agent Communication (Heterarchy)

The insight: The Hierarchy/Heterarchy paper argues that the neocortex's power comes from non-hierarchical long-range connections operating alongside hierarchical ones. C2A2 currently routes everything through the Master Agent — a strict hierarchy. Dense connections (Levin × Friston, Kastrup × McGilchrist) are forced through an unnecessary relay.

The change: Create agent-to-agent channels: a new directory wiki/lateral/ with one file per active pair (e.g., levin_friston.md, kastrup_mcgilchrist.md). Agents can write cross-tradition flags directly to their known partner channels. The Master Agent still reads all channels on each run — it doesn't lose visibility, but gains speed.

Pros:
- Directly implements the heterarchy insight from the paper we're tracking
- Speeds up cross-tradition signal propagation for known high-density pairs
- Reduces Master Agent bottleneck
- The Master Agent retains full read access — no information is lost

Cons:
- Could create noise if agents over-use lateral channels for weak connections
- Harder to audit: changes are now in N files rather than one inbox
- Agents need judgment about when to use lateral vs. hierarchical routing

Mitigation: Start with only the pairs that already have confirmed explanatory bridges (Levin × Friston, Kastrup × Friston, Stump × Levin, Kastrup × McGilchrist). Expand only after we've seen the signal quality.

Dependencies: None technically, but benefits from dispatch enhancement (Change 1) being in place first.

Effort: Medium — new directory, 4-6 agent prompt updates, Master Agent prompt update to read lateral channels.

3. Active Inquiry Cycle (Sensorimotor Learning)

The insight: The Thousand Brains paper's central claim: passive observation is fundamentally insufficient for learning. Agents must generate predictions, act to test them, and update their models. C2A2 agents currently only ingest and extract — they never probe across traditions.

The change: After ingestion, each tradition agent generates 1-2 cross-tradition hypotheses — specific, falsifiable predictions about what another tradition would say about the material just ingested. These are routed (via lateral channels or Master Agent) to the target tradition agent, which evaluates them against its own wiki and responds with CONFIRM / REVISE / REJECT + reasoning. The exchange is logged in both agents' wikis and in the cross-program index.

Example cycle:

Hawkins Agent, after ingesting the Thousand Brains paper:
  HYPOTHESIS for Friston Agent: "The Cortical Messaging Protocol between
  learning modules is an implementation of variational message passing in
  Friston's free energy framework. The modules pass approximate posteriors,
  not raw observations."
  → Friston Agent evaluates → CONFIRM (with citation to Parr & Friston 2019
  on neural message passing) → logged as CROSS-032

Pros:
- The single highest-impact change in this proposal. Transforms C2A2 from a knowledge recorder into a knowledge generator
- Directly implements Hawkins' core design principle: sensorimotor learning
- Cross-tradition hypotheses are the inter-tradition equivalent of a cortical column "moving its sensor" — each hypothesis reveals features of the inter-tradition space invisible from a single vantage point
- Generates the kind of specific, testable cross-tradition claims that the Pattern Detector is designed to evaluate

label: C2A2 Redesign Proposal — Thousand Brains Implications (Revised)
contentHtml:
C2A2 Redesign Proposal — Thousand Brains Implications (Revised)

Original: 2026-04-09 | Revised: 2026-04-10 | Incorporates 5 rounds of review feedback
Source: Deep read of Clay, Leadholm & Hawkins (arXiv 2412.18354)

Executive Summary

A structural reading of the Thousand Brains paper reveals that C2A2's agent architecture is — without having been designed that way — an implementation of the Thousand Brains Theory. The mapping is architecturally precise: tradition agents are learning modules, wikis are reference-frame-based models, dispatches are the Cortical Messaging Protocol, and the Pattern Detector is the voting mechanism. This accidental alignment means the paper's design principles can be read as an engineering spec for improving C2A2.

This revised proposal incorporates feedback from Tom's review of the original 6-change proposal. Key additions: tripling of tradition agents for intra-tradition consensus before cross-tradition dialogue; splitting Agent 14 into 14a (assumption extraction) and 14b (presumption detection); splitting Agent 15 into 15a (lit search FOR) and 15b (lit search AGAINST); a provenance protocol for chain-of-custody tracking across agents; a health metric r (intra-consensus / cross-survival, must be statistically >1); a developmental maturity model with stages 0-5; and the hypothesis that there may be a finite typology of cross-paradigm connecting memes.

Ten design changes follow, organized into six phases over approximately three weeks.

The Eight Design Implications

1. Dispatch Protocol Enhancement — "Reference Frame Location"

The insight: The Cortical Messaging Protocol specifies that learning modules send their hypothesized location within a reference frame. C2A2's dispatches currently contain what was found but not where in the tradition's conceptual space the finding sits.

The change: Add two fields to the dispatch format in all 11 tradition agent definitions:

Reference frame location: [which concept-space in your tradition this dispatch 
                           originates from — e.g., "basal cognition / collective 
                           intelligence interface"]
Conceptual bearing:       [directional signal — what question this dispatch is 
                           moving toward, phrased as a vector — e.g., 
                           "from substrate-independence → toward cross-scale 
                           goal-directedness"]

Status: IMPLEMENTED (Phase 0, April 10). All 11 tradition agent definitions updated.

Pros:
- Enables the Master Agent to build a spatial map of the inter-tradition conceptual space
- Makes it possible to detect when two traditions are "near" each other even if they haven't flagged a connection
- Low-effort, purely additive

Cons:
- Location data is semi-structured text initially, not coordinates
- Risk of over-engineering. Mitigated by observing what agents actually produce before formalizing

Dependencies: None.

2. Architectural Self-Awareness Layer (Agents 14a, 14b, 15a, 15b)

The insight: C2A2 is making design decisions daily, but the assumptions underlying those decisions are not tracked, and the unstated presumptions are invisible. The system needs a way to surface its own epistemic foundations and test them against existing knowledge.

The change: Six new agents forming a self-correcting loop with a decision point and long-term monitoring:

  • Agent 14a — Assumption Extractor: Reads session transcripts, extracts every stated assumption (things designers know they're assuming), maintains changelog, decision index, open questions, and daily metrics snapshots. Tags all output as ASSUMPTION (stated — designer was aware).

  • Agent 14b — Presumption Detector: Reads the same transcripts with an interpretive lens, surfaces unstated presumptions (things designers are taking for granted without realizing it). Classifies by type: structural, epistemic, normative, methodological, scaling. Tags all output as PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference). Runs after 14a to avoid duplication.

  • Agent 15a — Literature Search FOR: Receives testable items from 14a and 14b, searches existing literature for supporting evidence. Reports strength of support with citations.

  • Agent 15b — Literature Search AGAINST: Receives the same items, independently searches for challenging evidence. Steelmans the counterargument. Reports strength of challenge with citations. Flags systemic risks when multiple items share a common vulnerability.

  • Agent 15c — Net Evaluator & Dispositioner: Reads paired 15a/15b results and makes the disposition call: INCORPORATE (into validated premises register as operational self-knowledge), MONITOR (hand to 15d for periodic re-evaluation), or REVISE (flag for human review with specific risk assessment). Without 15c, the pipeline tests but never decides.

  • Agent 15d — Periodic Monitor: Manages two queues: MONITOR items on a weekly cadence (re-triggering 15a/15b searches until 15c changes disposition) and INCORPORATED premises on a monthly cadence (ensuring validated premises don't calcify as the literature evolves). Tracks evidence trajectories and escalates stale items.

The full loop:

14a/14b (surface) → 15a + 15b (test, in parallel) → 15c (evaluate & disposition)
                                                       ↓           ↓           ↓
                                                  INCORPORATE    MONITOR      REVISE
                                                       ↓           ↓           ↓
                                             validated_premises   15d      14a/14b + Tom
                                                       ↑        (weekly)
                                                       └── 15d (monthly re-check) ──┘

Status: IMPLEMENTED (Phase 0, April 10). All six agent definition files written. Provenance protocol spec written. First run pending.

Jeff Hawkins is the tradition's neuroscientist of intelligence architecture, offering a detailed, empirically grounded account of how the human neocortex actually works — as a hive-mind of 150,000 cortical columns, about 1% of which are active at any one time, each building its own complete world model based on sensorimotor experience.
